timeline.claim: NASA adds a mission: Artemis III becomes a 2027 test flight in low Earth orbit to rendezvous and dock with one or both commercial landers (SpaceX, Blue Origin); first landing moves to Artemis IV, targeted 2028.
Crew named: Randy Bresnik (commander), Luca Parmitano (ESA, pilot), Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio (mission specialists); backup Bob Hines; launch target 2027.
Artemis III Orion crew and service modules joined at Kennedy.
SLS booster forward assemblies with nose cones completed in VAB High Bay 3 (reported 2026-10-13).

NASA publishes the flight profile: about 14 days; Blue Moon Mark 2 test article in ~273-mile orbit; Orion docks, crew spends about two days inside it; Starship V3 test article docks with Orion for up to two hours, crew does not enter Starship; splashdown off California. Landings near the South Pole follow in 2028.
Artemis acceleration briefing at Kennedy: Artemis III flies to low Earth orbit in 2027; Artemis IV is the first Artemis landing; goal is a 2028 return to the surface.

corrections: Earlier draft said Starship stays docked about one day (secondary source). NASA (2026-10-23): up to two hours, crew stays in Orion.
